items.title: Why London matters: A world hub for commercial litigation
items.summary: In this video, James MacKinnon and Geoff Nicholas explain why London remains the leading global forum for complex disputes and how legal finance supports high-stakes litigation.

items.title: Litigation Finance Insider speaks with David Perla and Evan Meyerson about 2026 legal finance trends
items.summary: The latest edition of the Litigation Finance Insider newsletter surveys legal finance leaders on how litigation funding is evolving as the industry enters 2026, with a sharper focus on discipline, duration risk and realized performance. Learn more.

items.title: From legal costs to capital: The basics of legal finance
items.summary: In this video, Philipp Leibfried explains how legal finance transforms litigation from a traditional cost center into a strategic asset that unlocks capital, manages risk and supports business growth.

items.title: Disputes in Saudi family-owned businesses: Where risk really arises
items.summary: An in-depth analysis of family business disputes in Saudi Arabia, exploring minority shareholder rights, information asymmetry, Saudi Companies Law, arbitration limits and the role of litigation finance in restoring balance and preserving enterprise value. Read more.

items.title: Non-Billable covers Kindleworth's plans for US launch
items.summary: Speaking on The Non-Billable Podcast, the founders of Kindleworth set out plans to launch its first US office on the East Coast, pointing to growing frustration in Big Law and more favorable conditions for partners spinning out to form specialist boutiques. The founders highlight how improved access to capital and technology, including backing from Burford, has made law firm start-ups faster and less risky. Learn more.

items.title: The Lawyer explores emerging disputes trends for 2026
items.summary: The Lawyer interviews a range of partners, barristers and funders on the key trends they expect to shape the disputes market in 2026. The article includes perspectives from across the legal industry, with CEO Christopher Bogart commenting on increasing complexity in global disputes, the expected legislative response to PACCAR and growing interest in law firm equity solutions. Learn more.

items.title: Dubai and the future of legal finance
items.summary: Hannah Howlett explains her move to Dubai as a strategic decision that reflects the city’s growing role in global business, arbitration, and dispute resolution.

items.title: IAM examines the Unified Patent Court’s impact on legal finance
items.summary: IAM features an article in its recent Special Report on the strategic and commercial impact of the Unified Patent Court, examining what the UPC means for legal finance. The contribution, authored by Managing Director Christopher Freeman, explores how the new court may shape funding structures, risk allocation and decision-making in European patent disputes. Learn more.

items.title: Non-Billable features Burford's Kindleworth investment in "the moments that defined Big Law this year"
items.summary: Non-Billable includes Burford's minority investment in Kindleworth as one of "the moments that defined Big Law this year," stating that the investment "was another indication of the level of investor appetite in the [legal] sector." Learn more.

items.title: Evan Meyerson writes for European Financial Review about the value of legal finance for private equity
items.summary: Evan Meyerson, managing director who leads Burford’s U.S. Commercial team, writes in European Financial Review about why private equity firms should consider financing or monetizing legal assets, and how legal finance can unlock liquidity, reduce operating expenses, smooth earnings, and enhance exit valuations. Learn more.

items.title: ION Analytics reports on Burford Capital’s push into law firm investments and new markets
items.summary: ION Analytics reports that Burford Capital is targeting further law firm investments as part of a broader strategy to expand across new sectors and geographies. Learn more.

items.title: UK Government moves to reverse PACCAR decision, Global Arbitration Review reports
items.summary: Global Arbitration Review (GAR) reports that the UK Ministry of Justice will bring forward legislation to address uncertainty created by the Supreme Court’s PACCAR ruling and includes remarks from CEO Christopher Bogart, who welcomes the move as an important step toward restoring certainty in the UK legal market. Learn more.

items.title: Christopher Bogart featured in CDR's coverage of the UK government's intention to reverse PACCAR
items.summary: CEO Christopher Bogart was featured in CDR's reporting on the UK government's intention to reverse the PACCAR decision. Bogart says, "Restoring clarity around the enforceability of litigation funding agreements is an important step for the UK’s globally respected legal system, and we welcome the Government’s commitment to providing that certainty." Learn more.

items.title: Non-Billable writes about Burford's minority stake in Kindleworth
items.summary: Non-Billable writes about Pallas Partners, and how the firm is "one of a growing number of boutiques to launch with institutional-style infrastructure rather than traditional law firm back offices." The article notes that Pallas Partners worked "with legal consultancy Kindleworth on its setup, a model that has gained attention following litigation funder Burford Capital’s recent minority stake in Kindleworth as funders look for closer exposure to law firm economics." Learn more.

items.title: David Perla and Andrew Cohen highlight the value of legal finance for law firms and corporates in Corporate Disputes magazine
items.summary: Vice Chair David Perla and Managing Director Andrew Cohen are quoted in the latest issue of Corporate Disputes magazine, where they discuss the growth of the legal finance industry and the value it provides for law firms and businesses alike. Learn more.

items.title: The economics of litigation: A GC’s decision-making guide
items.summary: Burford’s Philipp Liebfried breaks down how GCs can apply economic discipline and legal finance tools to make smarter litigation decisions.

items.title: David Perla co-authors article in Carrier Management and Insurance Journal calling for clarity—not confrontation—between the legal finance and insurance industries
items.summary: In an article entitled "From Confusion to Collaboration," Burford Vice Chair David Perla and Parabellum Capital Managing Partner and Corporate Counsel Dai Wai Chin Feman co-author a piece for Carrier Management and Insurance Journal about how persistent misconceptions about claims costs and so-called "social inflation" highlight the need for clarity between insurers and the legal finance industry. Learn more.

items.title: Law.com International highlights Burford's presence in Spain
items.summary: Law.com International discusses draft legislation in Spain regarding class actions and highlights Burford's recent expansion into the Spanish market, noting that "Burford Capital, which manages a $7.5 billion portfolio globally, has already moved in, launching in Madrid in October with plans to expand." Learn more.

items.title: Original Jurisdiction spotlights how litigation can become a business asset
items.summary: David Lat, author of Original Jurisdiction, highlights the growing shift inside corporations to view litigation not merely as a cost center but as a source of profit. Learn more.

items.title: Burford CFO Jordan Licht discusses Burford's use of AI on CNBC CFO Council panel
items.summary: Burford Capital CFO Jordan Licht joined LinkedIn’s CFO for a CNBC CFO Council panel discussion with CNBC's Frank Holland, outlining how Burford is deploying artificial intelligence across the business. Learn more.

items.title: Nikkei spotlights Burford Capital and patent monetization opportunities in Japan
items.summary: Nikkei discusses patent monetization opportunities for Japanese companies, as well as the evolution of patent litigation in the age of AI, with CEO Christopher Bogart. Learn more.

items.title: Still the standard? How London can keep its disputes crown
items.summary: In this webcast, experts discuss how London can stay competitive amid rising global alternatives by adapting to evolving client needs around cost, speed and enforceability. Learn more.

items.title: Christopher Bogart writes for The Times about proposed restrictions in the UK on the legal finance industry
items.summary: In an op-ed for The Times, Burford CEO Christopher Bogart writes that efforts to restrict litigation funding are misguided and would ultimately harm consumers, businesses and the broader UK economy by limiting access to justice. Learn more.

items.title: CDR features Philipp Leibfried on the CAT's collective action regime
items.summary: CDR highlights growing consumer openness to class actions and notes that the UK regime is maturing, with experts pointing to recent landmark cases. Burford Capital’s Philipp Leibfried comments that the Competition Appeal Tribunal's (CAT) first-ever damages award in Kent v Apple marks a true “coming of age” for the system, signaling increasing confidence in collective redress. Learn more.

items.title: Manager Magazin highlights Chris Bogart’s insights on law firm equity
items.summary: German publication Manager Magazin explores private equity’s growing interest in law firms and notes that Burford Capital is helping to drive this trend. Christopher Bogart says law firms are showing "'growing interest'" in outside investment, and that "Burford has already invested in a UK firm while exploring similar opportunities in the US—positioning it as a key player in opening the legal sector to financial investors. Learn more.

items.title: Law360 Pulse writes that more GCs are "turning litigation into a strategic profit tool"
items.summary: Law360 Pulse writes that more GCs are "turning litigation into a strategic profit tool." Learn more.

items.title: Law.com International covers Burford's funding of a collective action in the Netherlands
items.summary: In its coverage of several collective actions against Booking.com, Law.com International mentions Burford's involvement in funding one of the claims on behalf of Dutch consumers. Learn more.

items.title: Financial Times spotlights Burford’s interest in law firm ownership
items.summary: Financial Times writes about law firm equity, describing Burford as pioneering legal finance, and mentioning its interest in buying minority stakes in law firms. Learn more.

items.title: CDR covers Philipp Leibfried's insights from the Global Class Action Symposium
items.summary: CDR's coverage of a panel at Global Legal Group's Class Actions Symposium includes insights from Head of Europe Philipp Leibfried on the Competition Appeal Tribunal (CAT), where he says that "the next stages of development for the CAT [rely] on getting good cases certified and settled faster." Learn more.

items.title: Evan Meyerson speaks with PE Hub about how legal claims can be valuable assets for PE firms
items.summary: In PE Hub, Evan Meyerson, managing director and head of Burford's US commercial investment team, highlights why legal claims should be viewed as valuable assets. Learn more.

items.title: South China Morning Post profiles Burford Capital
items.summary: Burford Capital is featured in the South China Morning Post, where CEO Christopher Bogart says that Hong Kong's "arbitration edge boosts legal finance." Learn more.

items.title: Nikkei features Burford Capital
items.summary: Nikkei interviews CEO Christopher Bogart, who notes that "AI will drive legal finance demand." Bogart focuses on the role of legal finance as it relates to intellectual property—especially in the technology and health care sectors—in the Asian market. Learn more.

items.title: Christopher Freeman writes in JUVE Patent about the UPC and the new economics of enforcement
items.summary: Managing Director Christopher Freeman writes in JUVE Patent about how the Unified Patent Court (UPC) is transforming European patent litigation, as well as the new economics of enforcement. Learn more.

items.title: The ABA Journal reports on Burford's interest in law firm equity investments | Burford Capital
items.summary: The ABA Journal, a publication of the American Bar Association, references Burford's desire to invest in law firms. Learn more.

items.title: Settle smarter: How data and valuation reframe high stakes disputes
items.summary: Burford and Solomonic explore how analytics and valuation modelling bring clarity and objectivity to settlement decisions.

items.title: Reuters reports on Burford's LegalTech Fund investment
items.summary: Reuters reports on Burford's investment in The LegalTech Fund, a "venture capital firm that invests in early-stage legal technology startups." The Fund announced it had closed a second fund at $110 million. Learn more.

items.title: Börsen-Zeitung highlights Burford's interest in law firm equity investments
items.summary: Burford's interest in law firm equity investments is mentioned by German publication Börsen-Zeitung. The article quotes Burford Director Jörn Eschment. Learn more.

items.title: JUVE quotes Burford Director Jörn Eschment on law firm equity investments
items.summary: Burford Director Jörn Eschment is quoted in the German publication JUVE on the topic of law firm equity investments. Learn more.

items.title: The American Lawyer interviews David Perla on how legal finance supports law firm succession planning
items.summary: The American Lawyer speaks with Vice Chair David Perla about the role of legal finance in law firm succession planning. Learn more.

items.title: Bloomberg Law highlights Burford’s innovative approach to law firm investments
items.summary: A Bloomberg Law analysis, entitled "Lit Finance Will Help Drive New Models of Law Practice," mentions Burford's interest in taking minority stakes in law firms. Learn more.

items.title: Legal Tribune Online features Christopher Bogart's recent Handelsblatt interview
items.summary: Legal Tribune Online (LTO) highlights CEO Christopher Bogart's recent interview with Handelsblatt. Learn more.

items.title: David Perla appears on Legal Innovation Spotlight podcast
items.summary: Vice Chair David Perla appears as a guest on Ted Theodoropoulos' "Legal Innovation Spotlight" podcast to discuss how Managed Service Organizations (MSOs) are reshaping what it means for law firms to innovate. Learn more.

items.title: Handelsblatt interviews Christopher Bogart about business in Germany
items.summary: Handelsblatt features an interview with CEO Christopher Bogart, where he discusses Burford's presence in Germany. Bogart says: "Germany is our largest market in Europe. We’ve been active here for more than ten years and work closely with German companies." Learn more.

items.title: Notices in Saudi construction disputes: How the Civil Code is shaping risk allocation
items.summary: As Saudi Arabia’s giga-projects expand, disputes over FIDIC notice compliance are increasing. Joe Durkin explains how the Saudi Civil Transactions Law is redefining contractual risk and fairness in construction disputes. Learn more.

items.title: David Perla speaks with The American Lawyer on the role of outside capital in law firm talent acquisition
items.summary: The American Lawyer explores the role of outside capital in law firm talent acquisition, with Vice Chair David Perla highlighting how management services organizations (MSOs) have strategic value in lawyer retention. Learn more.

items.title: Law360 previews the inaugural International Legal Finance Association (ILFA) awards
items.summary: Law360 highlights the inaugural International Legal Finance Association awards, which will be presented at the organization’s gala in London on November 13th. Nearly 50 organizations will be recognized for excellence in key areas including collection action, commercial litigation, funder representation, advisory services, arbitration, technology and law firm innovation. Learn more.

items.title: Chicago Lawyer writes about legal finance in Chicago
items.summary: Chicago Lawyer writes about the growth of legal finance in Chicago and the United States. Learn more.

items.title: Bloomberg Law highlights Burford’s innovative move to explore equity investments: “It takes just one out-of-the-box thinker...”
items.summary: Bloomberg Law's "Big Law Sportsbook" highlights Burford’s move to explore equity investments in major law firms—an innovative idea that is reshaping the conversation around law firm financing. Strom writes: “It just takes one out-of-the-box thinker…” to make this happen. Learn more.

items.title: 5 minutes with... Teresa Gutiérrez Chacón
items.summary: Spend five minutes with Teresa Gutiérrez Chacón as she discusses what drew her to Burford, recent trends in gas-related disputes and the way that legal finance is evolving in Spain and beyond.

items.title: The Korea Economic Daily discusses Burford's industry leadership
items.summary: The Korea Economic Daily writes about Burford's leadership in the legal finance industry and quotes Jonathan Molot, citing his comments in this year's shareholder letter: "'Our asset modeling is based on a vast amount of proprietary data. This allows us to precisely measure the risk and potential returns of the litigation we invest in.' He added, 'We're not simply a lender; we're a technology-driven financial firm that quantitatively analyzes and prices legal risk.'" Learn more.
